title: $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ for integral and rational coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, with valuation ring $\cO_E$. Use the condensed coefficient rings of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], pulled back to the small pro-étale site. Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme and $\Lambda\in\{\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb\}$. Then:

1. every constructible $\Lambda_X$-module has Tor amplitude in $[-1,0]$, and in $[0,0]$ if
   $\Lambda$ is a field;
2. every $K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ with cohomology in $[a,b]$ has Tor amplitude in $[a-1,b]$;
   hence $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)=\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and
   $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))=\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$.

The following counterexamples are over the scalar ring, or as constant sheaves on $X=\operatorname{Spec}k$ for a separably closed field $k$. For scalar complexes, perfect means isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]; for the constant-sheaf examples, perfect means locally isomorphic to such a complex of finite projective $A_X$-modules. For a finite nonregular ring the condition is essential: $\mathbf F_\ell$ over
$\mathbf Z/\ell^2$ is constructible but has infinite projective dimension. Finite Tor
amplitude is a condition on the whole complex: for $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^2$ the complex
$[A\xrightarrow{\ell}A]$ is perfect, whereas its nonzero cohomology modules are
$\mathbf F_\ell$, which are not perfect. So for every qcqs scheme $X$ and every finite commutative ring $A$
(with its discrete condensed structure), $\Dctf(X,A)$ is thick, but it need not be stable
under standard truncations (already for $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^2$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}k$).

proof.text: Put $R=\Lambda(*)$ and $I=[-1,0]$, or $I=[0,0]$ for field coefficients. The coefficient definitions identify $R$ with the stated scalar ring; the integral rings are DVRs by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. The integral coefficient map is flat by clause 1 of [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients]. Apply [lem-sfb-scalar-model-finite-flat-resolution] to each finite constant local model, then cover detection [lem-sfb-tor-interval-local-detection]. Thus every module with such a model on any scheme has interval $I$.
Apply [lem-sfb-stratified-tor-interval-devissage] to this common interval on all schemes. Its conclusion is clause 1 for every qcqs $X$.

For $K\in\Dbc$ supported in $[a,b]$, clause 1 and [lem-sfb-cohomology-tor-interval] with $[c,d]=[-1,0]$ give $[a-1,b]$. Hence every object of $\Dbc$ lies in $\Dctf$ by its definition, so the full replete subcategories agree. Their defining intersections for localizing closures are identical.

For finite discrete $A$, the coefficient ring sheaf is constant by the two finite-discrete coefficient identifications cited here. Finitely presented $A$-modules are finite, and finite modules are finitely presented (a finite free surjection has finite kernel). Thus finite constant local models are precisely finite locally constant models. The existing Serre-closure and triangulated-subcategory statements therefore apply to this constructibility predicate. A retract of a constructible cohomology sheaf is $\ker(1-e)$ for its idempotent $e$, hence constructible; its cohomological bounds persist. Thus $\Dbc(X,A)$ is thick, and intersecting with the thick class of finite-Tor complexes proves thickness of $\Dctf(X,A)$.

source.place: Final thickness clause; finite coefficient constructibility

proof.text: For $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^2$, $t=\ell$ satisfies $t^2=0$ and $\operatorname{ann}(t)=tA$, with $F=A/tA=\mathbf F_\ell\ne0$. Apply [lem-sfb-square-zero-periodic-tensor]. A finite projective resolution would give bounded tensor cohomology, since projectives are summands of free modules and thus flat, contradicting the nonzero self-Tor groups. The same calculation on every nonempty cover member rules out local perfectness of $F_X$. Its finite presentation makes $F_X$ constructible.

The complex $P=[A\xrightarrow{\ell}A]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ is perfect by definition, and $H^{-1}P=\ell A\cong F=H^0P$. Its finite free tensor complex has interval $[-1,0]$, so $P\in\Dctf$. Its truncations are $F$ and $F[1]$; the preceding unbounded self-Tor calculation and the shift rule exclude both from $\Dctf$. This proves all remaining counterexample clauses.

source.place: The examples, perfect complex and truncations
